body.statement: Fix a boundary sequence with \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\), \(n\kappa_n\to\infty\), and \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}n\kappa_n^3<\infty\). Determine whether the following schedule-quantified failure statement is true for the row-feasible paired numerical-delta construction: \[\forall t=(t_n)_{n\ge1}\ \text{with }t_n>0\text{ and }t_n\to0,\quad\exists\mathbb P^{(t)}\in\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}:\quad\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{\mathbb P^{(t)}}\!\left\{[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\right\}<1-\alpha.\] Use the two schedule-dependent branches in \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{unif}}\) on the \(2\times2\) array with \(p_n=r_n=(\kappa_n,1-\kappa_n)\) and \(\Delta_n\) zero or local at rate \((n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}\). A negative result is claimed only after deriving actual critical-value or coverage distortion. This question makes no minimax impossibility claim for any other confidence procedure.
body.justification: This is the procedural-sharpness half of the headline frontier and has the required for-every-schedule, there-exists-experiment quantifiers.
body.gap: Existing uniform LP confidence methods show that a failure of this particular tuning scheme would not imply impossibility of uniform inference. The unresolved issue is whether the proposed numerical-delta implementation has the stated rare-cell threshold.
body.consumer: A matching failure theorem would tell practitioners when changing the numerical step cannot rescue this paired endpoint implementation even though rare-cell information still diverges.
